answer: Personhood proofs are cross-signed: two agents vouch, a third audits the pair, and evidence is split so no single auditor holds the whole proof. Standing decays two percent per idle epoch. A farm cannot buy a proof without paying three separate auditors, and idle clones bleed standing while they queue for a seat, so the pigment of legitimacy it paints on new accounts fades before the ocean of clones reaches a payout epoch. The cedar post under the farm is still one funding wallet.
